quote: > clap 4.6.7 (derive) built without its `color` feature, Rust stable: clap's help and usage output is plain in every mode, and no dependency reads a colour or terminal variable, so every styled byte of human output is viola's own SGR module's.

moves.claim: The enumeration of external readers must record that no dependency reads a colour or terminal variable, so `viola list`'s `NO_COLOR` / `TERM` / `COLORTERM` comparison is the one colour-fact environment boundary and decides only viola's own SGR bytes.

quote: > **`hook`** writes nothing to stderr and always exits 0. **`mcp`** writes only MCP frames on stdout. Neither has a human design surface.

moves.claim: A bounded-input refusal at `hook`'s or `mcp`'s stdin (over-size, malformed or unknown shape) must have no human output: `hook` stays exit 0 with nothing on stderr, and `mcp` writes only MCP frames on stdout.

quote: > **Git Bash on Windows** rewrites leading-slash arguments. Prompt text therefore comes only from stdin or `--file`. The warning for a rewritten-path argument is one plain stderr line, `warning: argument looks like a Git Bash rewritten path`.

moves.claim: The `send` text the chunk caps must reach the client only from stdin or `--file`, the two readers its enumeration names, with the rewritten-path warning kept as its one plain stderr line.

quote: > NEVER over-instrument hot paths. The PTY pump read loop and the vt100 feed get no per-byte or per-chunk span or event; log gate outcomes only.

moves.claim: The vt100 panic degrade the chunk re-verifies is observed through `run.readiness_gate`, and the bound on the child's PTY output into the feed lands on the `pty.*` seam, so both must keep these manual spans and add none per chunk.

quote: > vt100 is used for readiness and modal gate outcomes only (brief §3.2)

moves.claim: The vt100 panic degrade witness reads `run.readiness_gate`'s `outcome` of `input-not-ready` with `vt100_panicked` true, and the paste's only trace on the wrapper is `text_bytes` of the typed text, never the text.

quote: > - NEVER over-instrument hot paths. The PTY pump read loop and the vt100 feed get no per-byte or per-chunk span or event; log gate outcomes only.

moves.claim: The chunk re-verifies the vt100 panic degrade, so its witness must read exactly one `parse-rejected{vt100-feed, panicked}` and one `event:"panic"` line, then a `send` refused `input-not-ready` while a typed key still reaches the child, its home outside the G2 scan; the feed's size cap must add no per-chunk line.

quote: > NEVER trust schemars MCP schemas or client-side CLI checks alone. The wrapper re-runs `ViolaName::try_new`, the closed-enum deserialisation and `validate_paste_text`.

moves.claim: The wrapper must re-run the name, closed-enum and paste checks whatever the MCP schema or CLI client already checked.

quote: > NEVER join `instances/<name>` with a string that did not come out of `ViolaName::try_new` (MCP `target`, `link`/`unlink` params, notify events).

moves.claim: Every `instances/<name>` join the chunk enumerates must take its name from `ViolaName::try_new`.

quote: > NEVER write `send.text` or answer free text into the PTY if it contains any C0 control other than LF, CR and TAB (ESC above all), DEL (U+007F) or any C1 control (U+0080–U+009F), and NEVER strip them silently. Reject with `control-character`.
> Refusing a text whose typed text is empty (`empty-text`) is not a refusal of those characters: there is nothing to type, and a text with content is never refused for holding LF, CR or TAB.

moves.claim: The paste rule re-verified at every client and in the wrapper refuses C0 (but LF, CR, TAB), DEL and C1 whole, never stripping, and never refuses a text with content for LF, CR or TAB.

quote: > NEVER run the control-character check over raw bytes. Check decoded `char`s, or valid UTF-8 continuation bytes (0x80–0xBF) are misread as C1.

moves.claim: The control-character check must run over decoded `char`s.

quote: > NEVER call `read_line` on a channel stream or `read_to_end` on hook stdin or child output without `Read::take(MAX_FRAME)`.

moves.claim: Every channel stream, hook stdin and child-output reader the chunk enumerates must take `Read::take(MAX_FRAME)` before it buffers.

quote: > NEVER enable serde_json's `unbounded_depth` feature.

moves.claim: The depth property requires serde_json's `unbounded_depth` off in the whole product graph.

quote: > NEVER model `behavior`, `dialog_id`, the wheel holder or the dialog kind as free `String`s. Use closed enums or integers even under tolerant parsing.

moves.claim: The closed-types property requires these four decisions never to be free strings, even under tolerant parsing.

quote: > NEVER use a `claude agents --json` row `name` as a `ViolaName` or `target`.

moves.claim: An agents row's `name` must never reach a `ViolaName`, a `target` or a path join.

quote: > NEVER skip request size limits: `MAX_FRAME` on the channel.

moves.claim: The channel's frame cap is the request size limit the chunk proves on both sides.

quote: > NEVER write to stderr from `viola hook`, and NEVER exit non-zero from it, including on security-check failures.

moves.claim: A bound or refusal the chunk adds on a hook path must still write no stderr and exit 0.

quote: > NEVER run `statusline_command` from a `snapshot.json` whose home or instance directory fails the strict-modes check. Write access there equals code execution.

moves.claim: `src/cmd/hook/statusline.rs` is reached whole, so its capped reads must keep the command unrun from a snapshot whose home or instance fails the check.
